manifest.name: agnes-ai-for-dsh
manifest.description: Agnes AI integration for DeepSeek Harness - LLM provider with multimodal support and GUI settings panel

bundle.text:
# Agnes AI Plugin for DeepSeek Harness
#
# Declares the agnes-ai provider for the llm-pi-ai adapter, plus the GUI
# settings panel. Users only need to supply their API key through
# Settings -> Models; DSH stores it in its own credential store.
#
# To use the Global endpoint instead, change baseURL below (or edit the
# provider in Settings -> Models) to: https://apihub.agnes-ai.com/v1

- id: llm-pi-ai
  config:
    providers:
      agnes-ai:
        displayName: 'Agnes AI'
        apiKeyEnv: AGNES_AI_API_KEY
        api: openai-completions
        # Default to the China endpoint.
        baseURL: https://api.agnes-ai.cn/v1
        defaultInput: ['text', 'image']
        # First install declares exactly these four models. The rest of the
        # catalogue is one click away: Settings -> Agnes AI -> 启用, which writes
        # this same array into the settings user layer through the panel.
        models:
          - id: agnes-2.5-flash
            name: 'Agnes 2.5 Flash'
            contextWindow: 524288
            # `maxTokens` on a model entry, not `defaultMaxTokens`: the latter is
            # a provider-level fallback. Inside a `models` entry it is an unknown
            # field, so it is ignored and the route default (32768) applies.
            maxTokens: 65536
            input: ['text', 'image']
            description: '免费·多模态对话·编码优化'
            systemPromptUpdate: in-history

          - id: agnes-3.0-flash
            name: 'Agnes 3.0 Flash'
            contextWindow: 524288
            maxTokens: 65536
            input: ['text', 'image']
            description: '免费·新一代 Agent 编程模型'
            systemPromptUpdate: in-history

          # Image and video models are only ever invoked by this plugin's own
          # tools (agnes_image_generation / agnes_video_generation), so their
          # provider entry declares nothing but identity: the `models` item
          # schema (PiAiModelProfile) requires only `id`, and the route's
          # `defaultInput` already supplies the modalities.
          - id: agnes-image-2.5-flash
            name: 'Agnes Image 2.5 Flash'

          - id: agnes-video-2.5-flash
            name: 'Agnes Video 2.5 Flash'

# GUI settings panel, plus the image/video generation tools.
- insert:
    - id: agnes-ai-settings
      name: 'agnes-ai-for-dsh'

readme.text:
Agnes AI integration for [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/dsh) —
an LLM provider with multimodal support, image/video generation tools, and a
settings panel.

[中文说明](README.zh.md)

| Piece | Description |
| --- | --- |
| **Provider** | `agnes-ai`, registered with the `llm-pi-ai` adapter (OpenAI-compatible Chat Completions) |
| **Chat models** | `agnes-2.5-flash`, `agnes-3.0-flash`, `agnes-2.5-pro`, `agnes-2.5-pro-beta` — all accept image input |
| **Tools** | `agnes_image_generation`, `agnes_video_generation`, `agnes_record_generation` |
| **Settings panel** | An **Agnes AI** section in Settings that lists the live configuration and the model catalogue, and configures models in place — one button per model, no hand-editing `cordis.patch.yml` |

The provider is pre-declared by `cordis.patch.yml`, so the only required step is
the API key:

1. Open **Settings → Models**.
2. Find **Agnes AI** and enter your API key.
3. The key is stored by DSH's credential system under `AGNES_AI_API_KEY`.

The default endpoint is the China region:

```
https://api.agnes-ai.cn/v1
```

To use the Global endpoint, change `baseURL` to
`https://apihub.agnes-ai.com/v1` either in `cordis.patch.yml` or directly in
Settings → Models.

A first install declares exactly four models, all free, in `cordis.patch.yml`:

| Kind | Models |
| --- | --- |
| Chat | `agnes-2.5-flash`, `agnes-3.0-flash` |
| Image | `agnes-image-2.5-flash` |
| Video | `agnes-video-2.5-flash` |

Everything else in the catalogue ships deliberately unconfigured — the two paid
Pro chat models, the older image model, and the paid video model. **Settings →
Agnes AI** shows each model with its state and the button that changes it:

Writes go through `ctx.remote.settings.mutate()` — the same Remote call the
built-in Models page makes — fenced by the revision the panel last read. A
concurrent change therefore answers `settings/conflict` and the panel asks you
to click again, instead of silently discarding one of the two writes.

Three consequences worth knowing:

1. **A write lands in the settings user layer**, which replaces the patch layer's
   `models` array wholesale. After the first button click, editing
   `cordis.patch.yml` no longer affects the model list until you press
   **恢复默认**.
2. **A language model is the only thing the provider can serve.** Image and video
   models are declared so the panel can track them and their ids stay visible;
   their entries carry only `id` and `name`, because a `models` item
   (`PiAiModelProfile`) requires nothing else. They also appear in the model
   picker, where selecting one as a chat model fails — they are meant for
   `agnes_image_generation` / `agnes_video_generation` only.
3. **The API key is not a model.** 一键配置 writes the provider declaration; the
   credential is still entered under **Settings → Models**.

Once enabled, the two media tools are available to the model:

- **`agnes_image_generation`** — text-to-image, image-to-image and multi-image
  editing. Parameters: `model`, `prompt`, `size` (`1K`–`4K`), optional `ratio`,
  optional `image` (input URLs), optional `return_base64`.
- **`agnes_video_generation`** — asynchronous video generation with polling.
  Parameters: `model`, `prompt`, optional `seconds`, `mode`, `size`,
  `aspect_ratio`, and the mode-specific media fields.

Video generation is asynchronous: the tool creates a task and then polls
`GET /agnesapi?video_id=…&model_name=…` until it settles. `agnes-video-2.5-flash`
accepts only `720P`; `agnes-video-2.5` accepts `720P`, `1080P`, `1K` and `2K`.

The host's `defineTool` does **not** accept raw JSON Schema — it requires a
property-map DSL whose entries may carry their own `required: true`, and it
compiles that into object-rooted JSON Schema itself.

That DSL is not valid JSON Schema. If it ever reaches a provider unconverted, the
provider rejects the **entire request** (WorkBuddy returns HTTP 400, code 11129,
"工具定义不合规"), so every model reply in the session fails — not merely the one
tool. This is not hypothetical: it is exactly what happened when a bare
`require()` threw inside an ESM module and a silent identity fallback registered
the raw DSL.

The defence is in `src/tools.ts`:

- `compileParameters()` compiles the DSL here, so the plugin does not depend on
  the host helper for correctness.
- `assertValidCompiledSchema()` / `assertAllToolSchemas()` verify the **compiled**
  form at load and throw on the invalid shape, so a mistake stops the plugin
  instead of poisoning every request.
- Registration re-checks the parameters `defineTool` actually produced and
  refuses to register if the raw DSL survived.
`verify.mjs` exercises all of this against the real `defineTool`.

readme.section: How the settings panel writes configuration
readme.text:
`src/client/index.ts` writes through the generated Remote namespace
`remote.settings`, and needs no seam of its own:

```js
writeSettings(NS, [{ op: 'set', path: ['providers', 'agnes-ai', 'models'], value: next }], revision)
```

`remote.settings` is reached through `ctx.reflect`, never injected, so a runtime
without it still renders the panel and a missing write seam reports its own
refusal instead of hiding the whole section.

readme.section: How the settings panel writes configuration
readme.text:
`unset` is the only operation that restores inheritance: an empty `set` would
mean "a route with no models", not "serve the default list".

readme.section: How the settings panel writes configuration
readme.text:
The pure helpers the buttons call (`enableModelOps`, `disableModelOps`,
`setProviderOp`, `restoreModelsOp`) are exported from the bundle, and
`verify-client.mjs` loads the bundle through a stubbed `__ModuleLoader__` to
exercise exactly those functions — including a cross-check that
`cordis.patch.yml` and `DEFAULT_MODEL_IDS` declare the same models, so the patch
and the panel cannot drift apart.

`defaultMaxTokens` is a **provider-level** fallback. Inside a `models` entry it
is an unknown field, so it is ignored and the route default (32768) applies
instead. A per-model output ceiling belongs in the entry's own `maxTokens`.

```bash
npm install
npm run build
```

`lib/` is committed, because the package installs from git and the consuming
profile does not run build scripts. **Rebuild before committing any `src/`
change**, or the stale `lib/` is what ships.

```bash
node verify.mjs          # compiled tool schemas vs the real defineTool
node verify-apply.mjs    # what apply() actually registers
node verify-output.mjs   # every tool result is lossless JSON
node verify-client.mjs   # the panel's read and write path, stub module table
